title: kate-core: build folds from line indent
summary: indent_folds returns half-open line ranges from leading indent. A blank line does not start or end a fold. This packet does not add a Command. It does not edit workspace.rs or indent.rs. Linux CI runs the tests.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust. It does not need a window or a review by the owner. Linux CI runs the tests. Also run cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub struct FoldSpan { pub start: u32, pub end: u32 }

#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn indent_folds(text: &str, tab_width: u8) -> Vec<FoldSpan>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: view.rs declares fold.rs with a path attribute. FoldSpan and indent_folds both use cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)). view is private and lib.rs is off limits. That attribute keeps clippy -D warnings green. A line starts a fold only when the next non-blank line has a greater indent. Indent counts spaces as 1 and a tab as tab_width. A width of 0 counts as 1. A blank line stays inside the current fold. end is the first later non-blank line whose indent is less than or equal to the start line. If none, end is the line count. Sort by start, then by longer span first. The nested example yields exactly 0..4 and 1..3. Do not fill View.folds. Do not edit indent.rs. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: fold::tests::nested_indent_makes_two_spans
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because indent_folds does not exist. A line starts a fold only when the next non-blank line has a greater indent. The text a, two-space b, four-space c, two-space d, e yields exactly spans 0..4 and 1..3.
